title: Vandyke stitch
subtitle: A raised central plait flanked by diagonal straight stitches
excerpt: Vandyke stitch forms a narrow band with a braided ridge running down the centre. Pairs of diagonal stitches are caught together with a central plait that builds up as you work, giving a raised spine well suited to leaf shapes and decorative borders.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Vandyke stitch entry.

content.text: Vandyke stitch works between two parallel guide lines with a centre line marked between them. Each step takes the thread diagonally to the outer edge on one side, then crosses to the other side. Before going under to make the next diagonal stitch, the needle slides under the previous pair of stitches at the centre without piercing the fabric. This interlocking pass is what builds the plaited ridge.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 3 to 4 strands for a visible plait

content.text: Mark two parallel lines and a centre line between them. Bring the needle up at A on the left outer line, near the top of the band.
Insert at B on the right outer line, level with A, and bring up at C, a short distance down the right outer line. Pull through.
Slide the needle tip under the AB crossing at the centre line from right to left, without piercing the fabric. Pull through gently so the thread locks across the plait.
Insert the needle at D on the left outer line, level with C, and bring it up at E, a short distance down the left outer line.

Slide the needle under the last two threads at the centre again, right to left, locking the plait. Continue steps 2 to 5 down the band, alternating left and right. Keep the central passes firm but not tight.

items.symptom: The central plait is loose or gaps appear
items.cause: The needle is not catching both threads of the crossing before pulling through.
items.fix: Check that the needle passes under the full X formed by the previous diagonal pair at the centre. Pull each pass snugly before moving to the next diagonal.

items.symptom: The side stitches are uneven lengths
items.cause: The outer turning points are not spaced consistently down the lines.
items.fix: Mark evenly spaced dots along both outer lines before starting. Keep each step the same distance down.

items.symptom: The plait drifts off the centre line
items.cause: The central catch is being made too far to one side.
items.fix: Always pass the needle through the crossing exactly at the marked centre line, not above or below it.
